entries.title: Geniatech Color E-Paper Partial Refresh Technology is Winning Awards
entries.summary: The company has new dynamic transition effects directly into the partial refresh process, allowing an e-paper screen to render animated transitions - including blinds, ripples, and gradients. The post Geniatech Color E-Paper Partial Refresh Technology is Winning Awards first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Geniatech has achieved a breakthrough in full-color e-paper interaction by enabling dynamic special-effect transitions during partial refreshes—a capability previously unavailable in commercial e-paper displays.

Geniatech’s engineering team aimed to rethink the conventional understanding of e-paper display capabilities. Leveraging an FPGA platform, they devised a novel method that merges 8-bit grayscale template-mapped phase shifting with a dual-dimension lookup table algorithm. This innovation allows dynamic transition effects to be seamlessly integrated into the partial refresh process, achieving a unique blend of “partial refresh” and “animated transition effects” not seen before in e-paper technology.

In practical terms, this advancement means an e-paper display can now update content without flashing the entire screen. Instead, it can showcase layered transition effects—like blinds, ripples, or gradients—confined just to the area where the content is changing, while the rest of the display remains still. This focused effect draws the viewer’s attention directly to the changes, significantly enhancing engagement and dwell time in retail and signage environments, all while maintaining the serene, paper-like readability that sets e-paper displays apart.

The innovation was recognized today with the 2025–2026 ePaper Creativity and Innovation “Pioneering” Award at the 4th ePaper Industry Innovation Conference in Shenzhen, one of the display industry’s most closely watched innovation honors.

However, Geniatech doesn’t appear to be licensing this e-paper technology to other brands; instead, it uses it in its own suite of digital signage, e-posters, bus stop signs, and e-paper displays. Most of their products use E INK Spectra 6, which is better suited to digital signage.

entries.title: Is the Amazon Kindle Colorsoft worth it in 2026?
entries.summary: If you rely on Kindle Unlimited or a large library of purchased Amazon books, Colorsoft is still the most seamless, optimized way to view color within that walled garden. The post Is the Amazon Kindle Colorsoft worth it in 2026? first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The Amazon Kindle Colorsoft 16GB edition is Amazon’s second e-reader. It was geared toward reading graphic novels, comics, or children’s books, or for readers who rely heavily on color-coded highlights and want to see book covers in color. However, the device recently underwent a huge price increase and is now $289 instead of $249.

Colorsoft is becoming less appealing in 2026, mainly because of stiff competition. The Kobo Clara Colour retails for $179.99, and it often goes on sale. Meanwhile, the Kobo Libra Colour is priced at $259.99, boasting the same 7-inch screen as the Colorsoft. However, it also offers page-turn buttons, double the storage capacity, and compatibility with a stylus—though the stylus itself isn’t included in the package.

PocketBook offers an impressive lineup of color e-readers featuring E Ink Kaleido 3 technology. This technology displays up to 4,096 colors alongside a sharp 300 PPI black-and-white resolution. Running on a lightweight, custom Linux OS, these devices support a wide range of digital formats without locking you into a single bookstore ecosystem. PocketBook Verse Pro Color normally retails for $159, the premium Era Color7-inch costs $259.99.

Unlike PocketBook’s lightweight custom Linux setup, Onyx Boox color e-readers operate on full Android (complete with the Google Play Store). This means you can install native Android apps like Kindle, Kobo, Libby, and Comixology directly onto the device. They utilize E Ink Kaleido 3 screens, providing 300 PPI for crisp text and 150 PPI for color content. The Onyx BOOX Go Color 7 Gen II E Ink Tablet is their latest generation device and costs $269.99. The Onyx Boox Palma 2 Pro is a premium, smartphone-sized color e-paper device that runs on Android 15. Released as a major upgrade to the standard monochrome series, its standout feature is cellular data support alongside a color screen, letting users stay connected on the go without relying on Wi-Fi. It costs more than the Colorsoft, but offers more value at $399.99 USD.

Whether you should buy the Amazon Kindle Colorsoft following the recent mid-August 2026 price hike depends entirely on how badly you want color media and how soon you need the device. If you rely on Kindle Unlimited or a massive library of purchased Amazon books, the Colorsoft is still the most seamless, optimized way to view color within that specific walled garden.

entries.title: Bigme Announces the HiBreak Dual 3 EINK Smartphone
entries.summary: The Bigme HiBreak Dual 3 delivers a revolutionary hybrid smartphone experience by letting you magnetically swap between an eye-friendly E Ink screen and a fluid color LCD panel, though its premium price and bulky dual-layer design may deter casual users. The post Bigme Announces the HiBreak Dual 3 EINK Smartphone first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The Bigme HiBreak Dual 3 is a newly announced hybrid smartphone that features a primary E Ink display on the front and a removable, magnetic LCD module on the back.

Officially unveiled in late August 2026, the device builds heavily on previous iterations by transforming the secondary display from a permanent, fixed screen into a detachable module. This modular approach gives users the eye-comfort benefits of an e-reader for daily use, while letting them snap on an LCD screen for dynamic content like video streaming and social media browsing.

The Bigme HiBreak Dual 3 stands out in the smartphone market due to its unique hybrid screen technology. The front features a color E Ink main display with an advanced 85 Hz refresh rate, which significantly reduces the lag and ghosting typically found on e-paper screens. Its most notable innovation is the detachable color LCD module on the back, which connects via magnets and metal pins for data and power transfer, letting users snap on a traditional screen for video playback or pop it off for a standard, distraction-free smartphone experience.

Additionally, the E Ink screen supports a 4096-level pressure-sensitive stylus, making it optimal for precise note-taking, sketching, and document annotations. Beneath its dual-screen exterior, the phone runs on a MediaTek Dimensity 8300 processor, delivering robust performance that is exceptionally high for an E Ink device. To complement this processor, Bigme offers the phone in two premium memory configurations: 12GB of RAM paired with 256GB of storage, or 16GB of RAM with 512GB of storage.

On the connectivity and software front, the HiBreak Dual 3 includes full 5G Dual-SIM capabilities for high-speed network access globally. The overall physical footprint matches its predecessor’s compact profile, with a revamped, minimalist rear layout featuring a streamlined, pill-shaped camera module with a single lens and an LED flash when the secondary screen is detached.

The phone runs Google Android 16 and has full access to the Google Play Store. No estimated price or release date is available yet; stay tuned to Good e-Reader for upcoming coverage.

entries.title: Hisense A10 and A10 Ultra EINK Phones are available now
entries.summary: Hisense has just launched the A10 and A10 Ultra E-INK smartphones with great hardware specs and a detachable color e-paper screen. The post Hisense A10 and A10 Ultra EINK Phones are available now first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Hisense has been teasing its new A10 E INK phone for several months, and it is finally available for purchase in China. There are now two models: the A10 and the A10 Ultra. They range in price from $476 for 8GB of RAM and 128GB of internal storage, to $576 for 8GB of RAM and 256GB of internal storage. The main difference between the regular model and Ultra is that the Ultra comes with the detachable color screen in the box.

Both phones feature a 6.13-inch Carta 1300 e-ink display with a resolution of 1648 x 824 pixels and a pixel density of 300 PPI. The phone only has a black-and-white e-paper screen. The screen supports 256 levels of grayscale and 36 levels of warm and cool lighting via the front-lit display.

One of the standout aspects of the Hisense A10 is the optional magnetic color screen. The 4.96-inch LCD panel attaches to the back of the phone using a magnetic ring and metal contacts. It can be attached or removed whenever needed. With the color screen attached, the A10 can be used more like a regular smartphone. Users can browse color comics, view charts and images, watch short videos, and use social media apps. You can simply detach it when you do not need it.

The A10 series is powered by Qualcomm’s QCM6690 octa-core processor, built on a 4nm process. The chip supports 5G connectivity and has been optimized for e-ink devices. Hisense says the phone can automatically reduce the processor’s frequency and power consumption during static reading. For demanding tasks, it can increase performance to keep the interface responsive. It has Bluetooth 5.1, WIFI, USB-C, and a 48MP main rear camera and an 8MP front camera. It is powered by a 4,000mAh battery.

Finally, the A10 series comes with Google Android 16, but does not have the Google Play Store. There are a handful of preinstalled apps such as WeChat Reading. However, users can sideload in their own APK files, so you can use Amazon Kindle or Overdrive Libby.

entries.title: First Look at the Bigme B6 PRO E-Reader
entries.summary: The Bigme B6 Pro is an ultra-premium, pocket-sized 6-inch color E-Ink tablet that acts more like an Android phone than a traditional e-reader thanks to its blistering 75 FPS refresh speed, massive 8GB RAM, and built-in 4G LTE cellular calling. The post First Look at the Bigme B6 PRO E-Reader first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The Bigme B6 Pro is an ultra-premium, pocket-sized 6-inch color E-Ink e-reader and paper tablet running open Android 14. Positioned as a heavily upgraded, top-tier alternative to standard compact e-readers, it differentiates itself by integrating 4G LTE cellular connectivity and exceptionally fast refresh algorithms.

The Bigme B6 Pro features a 6-inch Kaleido 3 color e-paper screen, presenting crisp monochrome text at 300 PPI and color content at 150 PPI. Boasts an industry-leading refresh rate of 75-85 FPS, drastically minimizing ghosting and enabling incredibly smooth web browsing, comic panning, and video playback.

The Bigme B6 Pro features a highly customizable 36-level adjustable dual front-light system. It uses white and amber LEDs on the side bezels to direct light across the screen, providing glare-free, paper-like illumination that emits zero blue light and remains flicker-free.

Under the hood is a MediaTek Dimensity 1080 processor, 8GB of RAM, and 256GB of internal storage. It also has a MicroSD card slot that supports up to 1 TB of additional storage. It supports dual-band Wi-Fi (2.4GHz / 5GHz) and Bluetooth 5.1. Built-in High-Definition HIFI stereo speaker and dual-microphone array with integrated GPT AI voice transcription. It is powered by a 2,100 mAh battery.

Supports an active capacitive pen that charges via USB for handwriting, sketch note-taking, and PDF document markup. Built-in local GPT artificial intelligence models capable of real-time multi-language voice transcription, text generation, document translation, and one-click meeting summaries. Bigme is using something very proprietary with this pen; we tried 15 different pens, and nothing else worked on the screen.

Android 14 OS with full Google Play Store support to download third-party apps like Kindle, KOReader, or Libby.

entries.title: Bigme Launches New E-INK Photo Frame
entries.summary: The Bigme E-Ink Photo Frame ecosystem represents a specialized lineup of cordless digital posters that function as glare-free, paper-like displays for home decor, scheduling, and digital art. The post Bigme Launches New E-INK Photo Frame first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Bigme has launched its new line of color E-Ink digital photo frames, featuring the compact 7.3- or 7.5-inch F7 and F7 Pro models, as well as the larger 13.3-inch F13. The company hopes to compete in this space against Pocketbook Inkposter, Aluratek ePaper 13.3, Philips Tableaux series, and the Samsung Color E-Paper EMDX Series.

While Bigme is widely known for its E-Ink tablets and e-readers, their “poster” line focuses on the Bigme F7 and F7 Pro Smart Digital Color E-Ink Frames. Rather than targeting massive commercial wall space like Philips or Samsung, Bigme designs compact, premium desktop frames that function as smart digital posters, weather calendars, and memos.

The standard F7 edition features an 800 x 480-resolution panel. It operates entirely cord-free via a built-in 1,300 mAh rechargeable battery designed to last for months on a single charge. It is available starting at around $123.28 CAD.

The Bigme F7 Pro is an upgraded HD variant utilizing a higher-density E Ink Spectra display. It bumps the screen resolution to 1024 x 600 with 158 PPI for significantly sharper text rendering and better fine-grain color saturation. It retails for around $137.13 CAD on the Bigme Official Store.

The Bigme F13 is a 13.3-inch smart color E-Ink digital art and photo frame. It employs an E Ink Spectra 6 Panel. It implements E Ink’s premium Spectra 6 full-color electronic paper technology, delivering a rich, highly saturated, completely glare-free print visual. Positioned as a significantly larger, premium upgrade to Bigme’s compact 7-inch desktop models, it transitions the ecosystem from a desk trinket into a proper wall-mounted visual poster or gallery showcase. The frame officially retails on the Bigme Official Store at a promotional price of $239 USD or regularly $289 USD

entries.summary: In this edition of the Good e-Reader Radio Show, we talk about Kindle Price Hikes, if Ad-supported Kindles now make less sense, and the new Pocketbook Q e-reader. The post Podcast: Amazon Price Hikes, Pocketbook Q and Onyx Picco first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Amazon has raised prices on its hardware devices like Echo, Kindle, and Fire TV by up to 60% due to a global memory and storage chip shortage. Amazon stated it delayed raising prices for as long as possible before updating its product line pricing. Kindle prices have increased anywhere from $30 to $60.

The PocketBook Q is a newly announced, smartphone-sized e-reader designed specifically to curb phone distractions and promote one-handed reading. Officially introduced in August 2026, the device ditches the wide tablet format of standard e-readers for an ultra-portable, pocket-friendly design.

The BOOX Picco is a micro-sized, pocket e-reader teased by Onyx in July 2026. It initiates an entirely new ultra-portable product category for the brand called the BOOX Tile line.

entries.title: Do Ad-Supported Kindles Make Sense in 2026?
entries.summary: With basic hardware now starting at $149, saving 13% by staring at lock-screen advertisements feels less acceptable to buyers, especially when competitors like Kobo offer feature-rich alternatives. The post Do Ad-Supported Kindles Make Sense in 2026? first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Amazon is the only company in the e-reader space that charges two different prices for its models; one with advertisements and one without. The ad-supported ones cost $20 less than the ones that do not show them. If you buy or are gifted an e-reader with ads, you can pay Amazon directly to remove them at a later date. Do advertisements make sense in 2026?

Amazon recently increased prices across its e-reader lineup, raising the basic Kindle to $149 with ads and $169 without it, while the Paperwhite jumped to $199 for the ad-supported version. Paying $20 less gets you an ad-supported device, but the ads are strictly limited to the lock screen/sleep screen. They never interrupt your actual reading. Ad-supported models show sponsored screen savers and require an extra swipe to unlock, whereas ad-free models can display your current book cover as the sleep screen and wake directly to your page.

With basic hardware now starting at $149, saving 13% by avoiding lock-screen advertisements feels less acceptable to buyers, especially when competitors like Kobo, Pocketbook and Onyx Boox offer feature-rich alternatives for comparable or better prices.

Amazon launched its Kindle with Special Offers back in 2011. It was a way to spend less when buying a Kindle e-reader for the first time. Kindle director Jay Marine said in an interview at the time that the release of a cheaper, ad-studded Kindle is Amazon’s way of getting the device into the hands of more people. But it also shows Amazon is getting more aggressive in its efforts to lure consumers tempted by competing e-readers and bombarded by ads for Apple iPad and a growing number of competing tablet computers.

What type of ads show up?

Most ads featured on the lock screen are house ads—promotions for books available on the Amazon Kindle Store, upcoming releases, or Amazon services. Occasionally, Amazon may feature external product promotions, but the primary driver is to steer you back toward making digital purchases within its retail network.

If you buy smutty books, these ads might occasionally lead to discovering new authors. However, when you take a Kindle out in public, you might not want these types of books to show up. Manga readers will also be inundated with all sorts of debauched content all over the Kindle. This prompted Amazon to launch an ad filtering system.

Amazon does not sell ad-supported Kindles in Canada because localized promotional campaigns and “Special Offers” infrastructure are primarily built for the larger U.S. retail ecosystem. Delivering localized, relevant book and retail ads requires specific regional marketing pipelines that Amazon has largely kept exclusive to larger markets, such as the U.S. and select European countries.

Wrap Up

I think that Ad-supported Kindles make less sense in 2026 following recent price increases, making the $20 savings less impactful compared to rising hardware costs and stronger competition.

Amazon plans to discount the Kindle e-readers back to their normal prices for the Prime Day Big Deals event in early October. This is the obvious test: if the discounts go deep, the ad tier stops looking quite so exposed.

entries.title: Kobo e-readers receive new software update
entries.summary: Kobo issued new software for its latest e-readers. They solved a lingering payment issue with their online bookstore and are laying the groundwork for Storygraph on older devices. The post Kobo e-readers receive new software update first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Rakuten Kobo e-readers have just received a new firmware update with advent of 4.46 for the Clara Colour, Kobo Clara BW, and Kobo Libra Colour. The main event is a new SSL certificate for the devices to connect to the online bookstore to buy digital content such as audiobooks, e-books, comics, and manga.

Before this new software, the current generation Kobo e-readers had problems paying for digital content on the Rakuten Kobo online bookstore.

Kobo e-readers have had Storygraph pushed out to their devices for a couple of months now. This new software is laying the groundwork to bring the functionality to older devices. This might result in the previous generation getting the social reading platform.
